7.4 Communication — One ticket, please 🎫

Aim: "I can buy a ticket." — the ss act out ticket dialogues (price, please/thank you, here you are).

Language: Can I help you? · Can I have a ticket to …, please? · That's … pounds …, please. · Here you are. · Here's your ticket. / Here are your tickets. · Thanks  ·  £ = pound

Quarter-lesson · don't / doesn't

don't or doesn't? — HELP! 🆘

"When do we say don't? When doesn't?" — they say first, then:

I / you / we / they + giraffes, snakes… → don't · he / she / it + a crocodile, a spider… → doesn't

Keep the button ritual: a stuck ss calls HELP, another ss answers before the reveal.

Quarter-lesson · practice — true facts!

True or false — and don't or doesn't? 🐘

Say the verb form — and check the fact. Stuck? Call HELP!

1 · Giraffes ______ eat meat. don't ✓
2 · A crocodile ______ fly. doesn't ✓
3 · Elephants ______ jump. don't ✓ (true!)
4 · A spider ______ have ten legs. doesn't ✓ (eight!)
5 · Whales ______ lay eggs. don't ✓
6 · A penguin ______ fly. doesn't ✓
7 · Snakes ______ have legs. don't ✓
8 · A kangaroo ______ live in Russia. doesn't ✓
Warm-up · books closed

Guess my after-school activity!

Books closed. One ss imagines something unusual they do after school. The class asks yes/no questions to find out:

"Do you go to the zoo? Do you play the piano? Do you…?" — "Yes, I do. / No, I don't." — 2–3 ss.

Books open. The lesson objective: "I can buy a ticket." 🎫

Lead-in

Where are they? 🤔

In pairs, predict: "Where are the characters?" — don't answer yet!

Pre-teach ticket 🎫 if necessary: "a ticket to the zoo, a ticket to the cinema."

Board support: the child deck, slide 2 — three guess-chips to tap.

Ex 3 · SB p. 88 · 🎧 3.28

Put the dialogue in order

📖 SB p. 88, ex. 3. In pairs, put the sentences a–f in order → compare with another pair.

🎧 AUDIO — 3.28 — listen & check

Check together — the correct order:

1 f · 2 c · 3 e · 4 d · 5 b · 6 a

f = Can I help you? · c = three tickets to the aquarium · e = That's twelve pounds sixty · d = Here you are · b = Here are your tickets · a = Thanks.

Language · prices

£ = pound — say the price!

£ = pound. £4.20 = "four pounds twenty" — we don't usually say pence.

Game 'Noughts & Crosses': a 3×3 grid of prices on the board — two teams. Say the price correctly → win your O or X!

Board support: the child deck, slide 5 — tap a square, the price in words appears.

Ex 4 · SB p. 88

Write how much it is 💷

📖 SB p. 88, ex. 4. The tickets (the page's numbers): 🦁 1 zoo £18.50 (the example) · 🏛 2 museum £8.20 · 🎬 3 cinema £9.30 · 🎤 4 concert £21.50.

Different ss write the answers on the board.

2 eight pounds twenty · 3 nine pounds thirty · 4 twenty-one pounds fifty

Board support: the child deck, slide 6 — the ticket cards, tap to reveal the words.

Ex 5 · SB p. 88

Roleplay — the museum 🏛

In pairs: buy a ticket to the museum. The prompts (SB p. 88):

A: help / you? · B: three tickets · A: £24.60 · B: here · A: your tickets · B: thanks

A: Can I help you? — B: Can I have three tickets, please? — A: That's twenty-four pounds sixty. — B: Here you are. — A: Here are your tickets. — B: Thanks.

Three more dialogues! 🎭

In pairs, act out three more dialogues — the tickets from Ex 4 (cinema £9.30 · concert £21.50 · museum £8.20) + the box phrases.
